column1: # The engine's layout: one row per script under `tools/loop/`, the bound the suite compares its length against, and the
# position the entry sources it at. Nothing is moved by this table — it describes the engine as it stands, so growth
# against a number someone argued for is a red case instead of a fact nobody measures (issue #890).
# `driver#everyEngineScriptIsInTheTable` reads the file column against the scripts themselves in both directions,
# `driver#noEngineFileExceedsItsBound` reads the bound, and `driver#theSourceOrderIsDeclared` reads the order.
# bound  the file's length when this table was written plus a quarter, rounded up: it records today's size and refuses
#        growth only, so raising one is a one-line diff with a reason beside it rather than a refactor.
# order  the position the entry sources the file at, or `-` when the entry does not source it. Every engine script
#        sources `lib.sh`, which is the whole of the order today.
# note   the order the move will use. `run-sh-is-split-along-the-stream` splits `run.sh` into owner files and adds
#        their rows beneath `lib.sh`, taking orders 2..n; this table is the one place that changes when it does.

column4: the split's files follow this row, at orders 2..n
the entry: it sources the order above and is sourced by nothing
